prompt:
Transparent atlas, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS AND ONE ROW. Four axis-aligned orthographic lateral edge elevations of one horizontal square diner checker floor tile, columns FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT, REAR. Each cell must be a low horizontal floor-slab profile at the same Z height and shared baseline, with broad tile-top checker pattern fully occluded. No top-down view in any cell, no tilted 3/4 views, no perspective. Consistent object scale and complete centered silhouette with transparent margin.

Faithfully use the supplied source tile's identity and palette: bold red-and-cream checker squares, a thin pale speckled cream stone underside band and narrow dark-gray metal edging/fasteners as seen around the tile perimeter. In these four elevation views the checker pattern should appear only as a hairline strip on the upper edge, never as broad facing panels; the main visible vertical side is the shallow cream-speckled stone/edge with dark narrow metal band and tiny fastener details matching the source. Keep the tile flat and horizontal; equal thickness across FRONT/RIGHT/LEFT/REAR. Preserve plausible square tile proportions, centered baseline, no detached pieces.

Negative: no broad checkerboard face in lateral cameras, no isometric angle, no slanted top plane, no tall upright wall, no extra border or steps, no color changes, no floor/background, no labels or dividing lines.
